Dubai: Classrooms are full again, offices are back to normal hours, and thousands of families have just returned from summer travel. All that mixing and close contact is exactly what lets flu spread fastest and it's why UAE health authorities have widened their vaccination push this year, with doctors urging residents not to wait until the coughs start. Recently, the Ministry of Health and Prevention (MOHAP) expanded its list of priority groups for this year's seasonal influenza vaccine, adding school students and pilgrims travelling for Hajj and Umrah for the first time. It's a signal, health experts say, that the window to act is now, before case numbers start climbing later in the year. Who needs the jab this year The full list of target groups for the 2026–27 seasonal influenza vaccination campaign is: Pregnant women Children aged six months and above School students Elderly people Those with chronic illnesses Healthcare workers Travellers performing Hajj and Umrah Vaccination is especially important for anyone at risk of severe flu complications, as well as those who live with or care for someone in a risk category. Flu, short for influenza, is a viral infection affecting the nose, throat and lungs. While the vaccine isn't 100 per cent effective, it significantly lowers the risk of severe complications, particularly for those most vulnerable. We can expect to see an increase in cases in the coming weeks and months, with December and January seeing more cases. Right now is the right time to receive the vaccine before cases rise during the colder months. It takes around two weeks for the body to develop protection against the flu.” At this stage, we are starting to see patients with influenza symptoms and respiratory infections, but it’s still an early flu season. We can expect to see an increase in cases in the coming weeks and months, with December and January seeing more cases. Right now is the right time to receive the vaccine before cases rise during the colder months. It takes around two weeks for the body to develop protection against the flu. Dr Malaz Yabrodi Specialist Internal Medicine at Medcare Shaikh Saqr Al Qasimi Hospital The Dubai Health Authority (DHA) guideline states that flu vaccination should ideally be given in September or early winter, before the influenza season begins. Dr Likha Rajan, General Practitioner at Aster Clinic, Al Wasl Village, said September gives residents enough time for immunity to develop before influenza activity increases. “Protection is not immediate, so vaccinating in September provides a buffer before increased community transmission. But if someone misses September, vaccination later is still beneficial while influenza viruses are circulating.” “September is an ideal time to take the annual flu vaccine because it allows approximately two weeks for protective immunity to develop before the influenza season increases.” Flu cases expected to rise from October Rajan said influenza activity for the 2026–27 flu season in the UAE is expected to begin increasing during the autumn months, with a more substantial rise generally occurring from October onwards and the highest activity often occurring around January and February. The UAE’s national seasonal influenza campaign runs from September 2026 through March 2027, reflecting this seasonal window. For the 2026–27 flu season in the UAE, I’d expect influenza activity to begin increasing during the autumn months, with the more substantial rise generally occurring from October onward and the highest activity often occurring around January–February. UAE health authorities’ national seasonal-influenza campaign runs September 2026 through March 2027, reflecting this seasonal window. Dr Likha Rajan General Practitioner at Aster Clinic What to expect in clinics September: Sporadic flu cases may already appear, but this remains primarily a prevention and vaccination window. October–November: Respiratory infections and influenza-like illness generally become more frequent. December–February: Expect the largest clinical burden, with January often the major peak. During the 2025–26 season, UAE hospitals reported a sharp rise in cases that month, according to Rajan. Dr Rajan cautioned that it's too early to predict this year's dominant strain or severity. "Influenza activity varies considerably from year to year, and surveillance during the season will give a much better indication," she said. Why children, elderly and travellers are being prioritised Yabrodi said vaccination is particularly important for people travelling for Hajj or Umrah, as well as elderly people and pregnant women, because of their higher risk of complications. “So for those travelling, especially those going for Umrah or Hajj, must get it at least two weeks before their trip to develop the antibodies.” “For those travelling, elderly and pregnant women it is essential for them to get the vaccine because there is a higher risk of complications and children can easily increase the transmission rate in schools and nurseries because of closer contact.” She added that elderly people may have weaker immune systems and are more likely to have chronic medical conditions, which can make influenza more serious. UAE expands seasonal respiratory disease campaign The UAE has also expanded its annual flu campaign this year to cover seasonal respiratory diseases. Under the new initiative, health authorities are asking two high-risk groups – pregnant women and older adults – to get vaccinated against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a virus that can cause pneumonia and bronchiolitis. RSV is a common virus that infects the lungs and airways, including the nose, mouth and throat. It usually causes mild, cold-like symptoms but can lead to more serious illness, particularly among infants and older adults. Needle-free flu vaccine option available In 2025, MOHAP introduced the influenza vaccine in the form of a nasal spray for the first time, adding a needle-free option to the approved vaccination choices for flu season. Since it is sprayed directly into the nose, the vaccine creates an immune response where the flu virus enters the body – the upper respiratory tract. For most residents, the message from doctors this month is simple: don't wait for the cough and fever season to arrive. September is the window — and it's closing fast. records.content: Alberta flu season is looming. Recent immunization numbers don't bode well, doctor says The number of doses was down, even though Alberta's population continues to rise. Only one in five Albertans got immunized during the previous flu season The 2025-26 influenza season was a doozy. The recorded number of seasonal flu cases in Alberta were much higher than they’d been over the previous four years. Thousands of H3N2 influenza cases were confirmed weekly, with the heaviest surge from November 2025 to January 2026. That must have led to long lineups at pharmacies across Alberta, right? The massive flu outbreak must have sent us all running to get immunized, correct? No. As Alberta endured its worst flu season in years, the number of immunizations was low. Province-wide, 1.035 million doses were administered in 2025-26. That was the lowest number of doses recorded on the Alberta Health dashboard, with numbers going back to 2010. The number of doses was down, even though Alberta’s population continues to rise. Only one in five Albertans got immunized during the previous flu season. In Edmonton, coverage was just above 21 per cent. So, if there’s a stereotype that rural immunization numbers bring down the average, the stats don’t bear that out. Both Edmonton and Calgary were just barely above the provincial norm. Across Alberta, 282 deaths were linked to the flu in the 2025-26 season. Of those, 92 were in the Edmonton zone. Dr. Louis Francescutti, a professor with the University of Alberta’s School of Public Health, said that our immunization rate should be north of 80 per cent. He said that high immunization rates are the most important indicator of a functioning health-care system. He said a 20-21 per cent vaccination rate is “pretty well non-existent” and that he expects emergency wards to be filled. “There’s not enough beds,” he said. “Just the other day, the Royal Alex went on an alert where there were no more beds to admit patients to, and that’s before the flu season even arrived. So, this is going to be a terrible fall for health-care providers.” - Alberta's top doctor urges Albertans to get vaccinated as flu cases surge - 'Measles capital of North America': Alberta doctors sound alarm on immunization - Advertisement 1Story continues below Pressing the point The province is still weeks ahead of the Oct. 5 rollout of the 2026-27 flu vaccine, but the Alberta government has already begun its media blitz. The vaccine will be available to all Albertans aged six of months or older at pharmacies across the province. And it’s free. “Fall immunization programs help protect Albertans from serious respiratory illnesses, protect more susceptible family and community members, and decrease the need for hospitalization,” said Dr. Vivien Suttorp, the province’s chief medical officer of health. “Additionally, this reduces pressures on our health-care system.” “By expanding protections and offering immunization options close to home, we’re giving families more ways to protect the people they love, especially those most vulnerable,” said Alberta’s Primary and Preventative Health Services Minister Justin Wright. The COVID effect While flu shots are free, COVID-19 shots have many Albertans paying out of pocket. COVID-19 shots are available at pharmacies for Albertans 12 years of age and over, and cost $100 per jab unless the patient qualifies for a publicly funded booster. To qualify for the free dose, a person must be at increased risk of an underlying illness or live in a “congregate living” home. Free shots are also available to First Nations, Inuit and Metis. They are also free for seniors, pregnant patients and the homeless. Teachers and health-care workers are also eligible to have the $100 charge waived. Fewer than 440,000 COVID-19 shots were administered during the 2025-26 flu season, almost half of what they were two years ago when they were available free of charge. In 2020-21, during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, the number of flu vaccinations hit its peak, with 37 per cent of the population getting inoculated for influenza. So, the numbers tell us there was a correlation — since Albertans were already going to pharmacies to get COVID-19 shots, they were getting influenza jabs, too. Now that COVID-19 vaccination numbers have plummeted, so have influenza vaccinations. Why aren’t we getting immunized? The Canadian Medical Association (CMA) lists four reasons why people are “vaccine hesitant.” They are: - Concerns over vaccine safety - Lack of trust - Complacency - Misinformation While these are listed as four separate reasons, three of them are linked. Concerns over safety, trust issues and misinformation all go hand in hand. “False information, often let loose on social media, amplifies and exaggerates the above issues,” stated the CMA in its report. The CMA also found that people who don’t have family doctors are more likely to go online for medical information or to self-diagnose. And that has the potential to expose them to a world of misinformation. So, there is a link between the lack of family physicians taking new patients and vaccine acceptance. Francescutti said the province isn’t doing enough to get people to trust the advice of health-care professionals. “I think people have become vaccine-hesitant, and there’s been a little bit of burnout with the COVID vaccines, and unfortunately, flu sort of got caught in that whole milieu,” he said. “Then there’s a whole new population out there that doesn’t believe in vaccines. There’s a lot of anti-science, and so what’s ending up happening is the perfect storm.” Invincibility complex But while misinformation is a problem, complacency is an even larger one. The CMA’s report says that because vaccines tend to work so well, we take them for granted. “Ironically, the very success of vaccines over time has led some people to believe that they’re no longer necessary,” stated the CMA. “Respondents to some studies have said that vaccines are not needed because they rarely contract infectious diseases or their immune systems are able to handle any infection.” Francescutti has given up on trying to get the antivax crowd to reconsider their choices. “When I see parents that don’t want to immunize their kids anymore, I don’t try and change their minds,” he said. “I just tell them what to look for when their kid is really ill, and then I say, ‘Listen, you didn’t immunize your child against the following diseases. records.content: AIFA Flu: nine vaccines approved for the new season, including a nasal spray for children The Department of Health recommends that regional flu vaccination campaigns be launched from the start of October. Here is the list of authorised vaccines by Health Editorial Team 16 September 2026 Aggiungi Il Sole 24 Ore ai preferiti su Google ANSA 3' min read Translated by AI Versione italiana Key points Consolidated security profile Who is eligible for the free vaccine The decision lies with the regions 3' min read Translated by AI Versione italiana There are nine vaccines authorised by AIFA and the European Medicines Agency for immunisation against seasonal influenza. As is the case every year, the authorisation involves updating the viral strains based on the antigenic characteristics of the strains circulating during the previous season, in accordance with the recommendations of the World Health Organisation (WHO). The vaccines authorised for the 2026–2027 flu vaccination programme are as follows: - Efluelda (Sanofi), injectable suspension: indicated for the active immunisation of adults aged 60 and over. - Fluad (Seqirus), adjuvanted, suspension for injection: indicated for the active immunisation of adults (aged 50 years and over). - Fluarix and Fluarix Tetra (GlaxoSmithKline), suspension for injection: indicated for the active immunisation of adults and children from 6 months of age. - Flucelvax (Seqirus), suspension for injection: indicated for the active immunisation of adults and children from 6 months of age. - Fluenz (AstraZeneca) nasal spray: indicated for active immunisation in children and adolescents aged between 2 and 18 years. - Influvac S and Influvac S Tetra (Viatris), suspension for injection: indicated for the active immunisation of adults and children from 6 months of age. - Vaxigrip (Sanofi), suspension for injection: indicated for the active immunisation of adults, including pregnant women, and children from 6 months of age. Vaccination of pregnant women extends protection to infants from birth up to 6 months of age (passive protection). Loading... Proven security track record “Flu vaccines have been used for years in vaccination campaigns and have a well-established safety profile”, notes the Agency, which monitors vaccine safety and, through the National Pharmacovigilance Network (RNF) with the support of regional centres, collects and analyses reports of suspected adverse reactions from healthcare professionals and members of the public. The data is also shared with the EMA to ensure coordinated monitoring at European level. In its circular entitled ‘Prevention and control of influenza: recommendations for the 2026–2027 season’ dated 23 June 2026, the Ministry of Health recommends ‘conducting regional flu vaccination campaigns from the start of October (week 40 of the year) and to offer the vaccination to eligible individuals at any time during the influenza season, even if they arrive late for their vaccination or report having already had one or more flu-like episodes. This may be particularly important in the event of a late flu season or when high-risk patients present for vaccination”. Who is entitled to a free vaccine “Vaccination is recommended and actively offered free of charge to everyone aged 60 and over,” emphasises AIFA, “as well as to pregnant women and those in the postnatal period, children aged between 6 months and 6 years, to those with medical conditions that put them at greater risk of complications from influenza, to residents of long-term care facilities, to family members of individuals at high risk of complications, to staff in public services of primary public interest (such as doctors and healthcare and social care staff, police officers and firefighters), other categories of socially essential and particularly exposed workers, workers in contact with animals that could be a source of infection with non-human influenza viruses, and other categories such as blood donors”. The decision rests with the regions Not all authorised vaccines are necessarily available on the market. Each year, the regions decide, through tenders for supply, which of the commercially available products will be used during vaccination campaigns and provided free of charge by the National Health Service. Vaccination is the most effective way of preventing flu and its complications, concludes AIFA, pointing out that, in addition to vaccine-based prevention and treatment measures, “an important measure in limiting the spread of influenza is good hygiene practices such as hand hygiene (washing your hands regularly and frequently with soap and water) and the containment of respiratory secretions (covering your mouth and nose with a tissue when coughing or sneezing and then disposing of it in the bin; regularly ventilating the rooms you are in)”. For Seniors, September Is the Time to Plan for Flu Season communityCommunity HealthHealth For Seniors, September Is the Time to Plan for Flu Season By Conviva Senior Primary CareSeptember 17, 2026 Smiling healthy mature older senior happy woman showing bandage on arm after getting vaccination. Vaccine and old elder people inoculation, elderly immunity for covid prevention concept. Portrait Even though the weather may still be warm, September is an important time for seniors to start thinking about something that may not be top of mind yet: flu season. That’s because what may be a routine seasonal illness for many can be more serious for adults 65 and older. As we age, our immune defenses are not as robust, and since many seniors also live with chronic conditions – such as diabetes, heart disease or respiratory disease – there’s a greater chance of complications from influenza. A Good Time to Get Protected For most older adults, September and October are generally good times to get the flu shot. Getting vaccinated too early in the summer may mean protection can wane before flu activity is at its highest, while waiting too long can leave one unprotected as influenza season begins. Up to 85% of seasonal flu-related deaths and more than half of flu-related hospitalizations have occurred among adults 65 and older in recent years. (CDC) Flu vaccination is effective because it not only reduces risk of getting flu, but can help reduce the severity of the virus for those who do become sick. Setting the Record Straight To be clear, the flu shot does not cause or give you the flu. Some people do experience temporary shot side effects, such as soreness at the injection site, fatigue, headache or muscle aches. These effects are generally mild and short-lived compared with the potentially serious complications of influenza. Seniors should focus less on whether a vaccine might cause a day of discomfort and more on its ability to prevent serious illness. Prevention Doesn’t End with a Vaccine A flu shot is an important first step, but seniors can take additional measures to protect themselves throughout the season. Wash your hands regularly, avoid close contact with people who are sick, and consider wearing a mask in crowded settings when respiratory viruses are circulating heavily. Staying well hydrated, getting adequate sleep and maintaining healthy routines also can support well-being. It’s also important for seniors to stay up to date on other recommended vaccinations, including those that protect against respiratory illnesses and pneumonia. Your Conviva primary care provider can review your vaccination history and help determine what is appropriate for you. Part of Your Fall Routine September is an ideal time to put flu prevention on your calendar. Don’t wait until influenza is spreading throughout your community to start thinking about protection. Getting a flu shot can be affordable and accessible. For many patients with eligible benefits and coverage, the flu vaccine is available at no out-of-pocket cost. A few minutes spent preparing now can make a meaningful difference later. records.content: 顶部 首页 首页 晴 / 21° 隐私 流感疫苗怎么选?网传“4价苗消失”到底咋回事?江苏疾控发文解答 新华日报 深入探索 车辆和载具 体育 电视与视频 根据全国急性呼吸道传染病哨点监测情况(2026年第36周)监测数据显示,全国流感整体处于低至中等流行水平, 近期呈现小幅上升趋势,南方省份检测阳性率高于北方省份,处于中流行水平。流感病毒已成为当前呼吸道感染首要高发病原,超过新冠、鼻病毒等其他呼吸道病毒。本轮流感以甲型流感为主(67.1%,其中H3N2亚型占甲型流感病毒的95.9%),同时合并B(Victoria)(32.9%),两种毒株共同流行。 尽早带孩子和家中老人接种接种流感疫苗是很多家庭防护流感的选择。问题来了:流感疫苗选几价?最近好多人说找不到4价流感疫苗,是怎么一回事?江苏疾控一次性讲明白。 一、先搞懂: 流感疫苗“几价”是什么意思? 简单一句话:几价=疫苗能预防几种流感病毒亚型 3价流感疫苗:预防2个甲型流感毒株 + 1个乙型流感毒株(甲H1N1 + 甲H3N2 + 乙Victoria系) 4价流感疫苗:预防2个甲型流感毒株 + 2个乙型流感毒株(上面 3 种 + 乙Yamagata系) 甲型流感传染性强、容易引发大流行;乙型流感常造成局部暴发。4价比3价多覆盖一种乙型流感毒株,防护范围更广一点。 展开剩余 78 % 小提醒:每年WHO会预测下一季流行毒株,疫苗生产企业按照推荐毒株来生产疫苗,毒株每年都会更新。 二、今年为啥没有4价 这个选择了? 图源:网络 是的没有四价了。 注意看,少掉的是 B/Yamagata 系,它已经好几年没出现了。 世界卫生组织(WHO) 监测数据显示自2020年3月以来,全球流感监测网络已经连续多年未检测到自然流行的B/Yamagata系病毒,不再推荐将B/Yamagata系抗原纳入疫苗组分。 三、别的疫苗打一次就管好久, 为什么流感疫苗, 每年都要折腾一回? 两个原因。 1.流感病毒太爱「变异」了 这里涉及到一个黑话叫「抗原漂移」。 流感病毒在传播过程中,负责编码血凝素(HA)和神经氨酸酶(NA)的基因发生点突变。 累积到一定程度,病毒的外貌就变得让人认不出来了。 就像手机里存了一张通缉照,但嫌疑人每年都「变脸」,得每年更新照片才行。 这也是为什么流感疫苗不能像麻疹、乙肝等疫苗那样打一次管好多年。 2.体内的抗体会「过期」 我们接种流感疫苗后产生的保护性抗体水平会随时间衰减,一般可维持 6~8 个月。 四、接种方式, 挨针 VS 喷鼻子? 按接种方式,目前主要有两大类,大家可按需选择: 1.打针的 通过肌内注射,也就是我们最熟悉的打胳膊形式。 适用于 6 月龄及以上人群,包括0.25mL(6月龄-3岁)和0.5mL(3岁及以上)两种剂型。 优点是:适用人群广,接种方式简易。 2.鼻喷的 通过鼻腔喷雾接种,在两侧鼻孔各喷一下。 适用于3-17岁人群,怕打针的“宝宝”可以考虑。 但鼻喷有禁忌,以下情况不能用: 鼻喷禁忌症清单* 家长必看 1因使用药物、艾滋病毒感染等任何原因造成免疫功能低下者 2长期使用含阿司匹林或水杨酸成分药物治疗的儿童及青少年 32~4 岁患有哮喘的儿童 4妊娠女性 5有格林-巴利综合征病史者 6接种前 48 小时使用过奥司他韦、扎那米韦等抗病毒药物者,或接种前 5 天使用过帕拉米韦,或接种前 17 天使用过巴洛沙韦者。 *具体参照相关《疫苗说明书》及《中国流感疫苗预防接种技术指南(2026—2027)》或者直接咨询接种医生。 温馨提示:如果你对流感疫苗所含任何成分(包括辅料、甲醛、裂解剂及抗生素)过敏者,或有过任何一种流感疫苗接种严重过敏史者,禁止接种。 最后,提醒大家,尽早接种! 流感黄金接种时机是 9~10 月。为什么是这个时间? 因为接种后大约需要 2~4 周才能产生足够抗体。而流感高峰通常在12月 ~ 次年2月。 算下来,10月底前打好,刚好赶上高峰期前产生保护。 Free web novels for online reading. 评论 全部 还没有人评论过,快来抢首评 抢首评 深入探索 艺术与娱乐 新闻 电视与视频设备 推荐阅读 王晶爆张国荣跳楼内幕!抑郁症只是一方面,受内地金主影响最大 玄真八字命... 2026.8.30 64.5万+ 摸腚女迎来大结局,央广网揪出幕后“帮凶”,这下又有人脸红了 淡墨绘江南 前天09:55 67.2万+ “开一次房,就下一单”,男子和女销售开房180次,7年购买上千万保险 江山挥笔 2026.8.23 1123.4万+ 两性关系:74岁大妈实话实说,男性过了68岁 对女人最大需求有5个 暧心情感 昨天15:09 1.2万 “台湾永远都不会回归中国,只要我在,就会抗战到底”,这句话曾出自2023年,台独分子林淑雅的口中,然而就在她说完没多久,当场被砸身亡。” 锋火局事 2026.8.31 286.0万+ 敬一丹病逝4天!丈夫王梓木私生活被扒底朝天,他大概率不会再婚 松庐衍 5天前 8.3万 甜美微笑太治愈!温柔小姐姐的侧颜杀谁能顶得住呀? records.content: Flu season is upon us and here's how you can protect your loved ones How-to News Well-being Written by: Shifali Jain 16th September 2026 It’s that time of the year again where flu season takes over the city This is a tale as old as time – every year, as winter approaches, there’s this impending doom of the flu season looming over us. Not ideal, we know. It is a signifier of the best season that is yet to bestow upon us (aka winters in Dubai ) yet is always followed by the worst symptoms of sore throat, fevers, a runny nose – rarely anyone gets spared from this phenomenon (the What’s On team included). But here’s how you can keep yourself and those you love safe from virus. If you haven’t heard already, influenza is in the air. And to prevent the virus from winning, UAE health authorities are urging residents to take measures to keep their families safe as well as take the yearly influenza vaccine. Vaccinations are now available to the public, starting from ages 6 months. Why do you need a shot of the vaccine? In a recent campaign launched by the The Ministry of Health and Prevention (MoHAP) – National Seasonal Influenza Awareness Campaign for 2026–2027 aims to raise awareness for the seasonal viral infections. The slogan “Protect Yourself... Protect Your Community” stands as the ultimate testament to what is required of the public. Beginning from September 1 through March 31, 2027, the campaign aims to increase awareness on the precaution and prevention of the spread of influenza, particularly amongst people who are at a higher risk of complications. The influenza vaccine is available to everyone in the UAE from kids who are 6 months of age to older adults, pregnant women, people with chronic diseases and weakened immune systems, children and healthcare workers. Basically anyone and everyone is recommended to take the shot in preventing the spread of the virus. Now, the health authorities also recommend the public to take these vaccines yearly as the virus is notorious known for evolving overtime and may become resistant to previous shots. How else can you protect those around you from the seasonal flu? Prevention is the easy part, and it’s also the best way for you to protect those around you. So what steps must you take to avoid getting infected or passing it on to those who might be slightly vulnerable to the virus. Make sure you wash your hands regularly. More specifically after you’ve sneezed or coughed or use an alcohol-based sanitizer. Avoid touching your face Disinfect surface areas regularly Make sure indoor spaces are well ventilated Use a mask if need be Make sure you eat a balanced diet. Don’t skip out on your daily dosage of vitamin supplements.
